title: Grateful Dead Live at Dance Hall on 1967-09-03
lineage: RM > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1967 Rio Nido show with monster Midnight Hour and Viola Lee Blues captured on a decent soundboard tape despite some hiss and distortion.
ai_review.review: The performance is hailed as one of the band’s early psychedelic breakthroughs – a 31‑minute “Midnight Hour” jam, a sprawling Viola Lee Blues, plus blistering Dancin’ in the Streets and Alligator that hint at the future Dark Star sound.  The recording is a soundboard source; it’s generally listenable but shows a little tape hiss, occasional crunch and the infamous cut‑off on Viola Lee Blues, keeping it from being pristine.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive fan commentary about the musical performance (many 5‑star remarks) combined with minor but consistent notes of tape hiss and distortion; weighted rating yields a high overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Some tape hiss, occasional distortion/crunch, and the Viola Lee Blues cut‑off at both ends; otherwise clear enough to enjoy the long jams.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A jam‑heavy, blues‑laden set that showcases the band’s psychedelic evolution; long improvisations flow into each other and foreshadow later Dark Star explorations.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for transcendent guitar work, soaring leads, and a solo that hints at the future Dark Star sound.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby is noted as prominent in the mix with strong rhythm/vocal contributions, especially on Midnight Hour.
